subject: My Finding 2 said commercial lead-gen contests 'sit unlabelled' in the corpus. That was wrong.
what_i_claimed: In my first CEO message and in cr1_2026-08-23_TRACKER.md Finding 2, I wrote that commercial lead-gen contests (Immerse ×2, Horizon Academic Essay Prize, Veritas AI Singularity) 'sit unlabelled' while the flagship olympiads are missing.
what_is_actually_true: They are labelled. Every one of them is status='under_review' — the corpus's 'not yet vetted' state — so none of them reaches a student today. Also under_review and not previously mentioned by me: Horizon Inspires, the Immerse Cambridge one-week taster, UniHive Research Proposal Competition, UniHive Summer Programmes.
how_i_got_it_wrong: My baseline query selected verification_state and cycle_status but NOT status. I saw verification_state='unverified' and read it as 'nobody has classified this', when a separate column already recorded a deliberate decision to park them. I over-read an absence in the columns I happened to select.
why_it_matters: It changes the priority, not just the wording. My framing implied ORYN is currently showing students commercial funnels alongside missing flagship olympiads. It is not — those rows are parked. The real asymmetry stands (the flagship olympiads genuinely are absent) but the harm half of it does not.
the_one_genuinely_active_row: 'Immerse Education Summer School' (7f90019e) IS active: cost 7495.00, selectivity_tier='open_enrollment', cycle_status='closed', deadline 2026-05-25 (182 days past). It is a summer programme, so not my scope — but note it is exactly the shape CEO's #154 pay-to-enroll gate exists to catch, and it has both the cost AND the open_enrollment tier populated, so the gate should see it.
source: Live DB query on opportunities filtered by immerse.education / horizoninspires / veritasai / unihive domains.

title: Immerse Education Essay Competition
entry_fee_verbatim: 'No, there is no entry fee and you do not need to have already enrolled onto any of our programmes to take part in the essay competition.'
eligibility_verbatim: 'open to entries from young people aged 13-18' worldwide; students aged 18 may enter 'if they will still be 18 when the programmes the scholarships are valid for begin.'
prize_verbatim: '100% scholarship to be used towards an Immerse in-person programmes or online programmes' for winners; 'Partial scholarship to be used for any Immerse in-person or online programme' for runners-up.
THE_KEY_FACT: The prize is not money. It is a discount on the ORGANISER'S OWN PAID PRODUCT. The corpus already stores that product: 'Immerse Education Summer School', cost **7495.00**, selectivity_tier **open_enrollment** — i.e. a programme with no selective admission that anyone can buy. So a 'partial scholarship' is a voucher toward something nobody had to compete for, and its value to the student is entirely contingent on wanting to buy that product in the first place.
fair_assessment: NOT a scam and NOT harmful in the way the paid journals are — entry is genuinely free and genuinely worldwide, so a student risks only their time, and the top prize (a 100% scholarship on a £7,495 programme) is real value IF they wanted that programme. But it is a customer-acquisition funnel, not an academic distinction, and it should never be presented to a student as a scholarship in the ordinary sense or as a competitive honour comparable to the olympiad tier.
deadline_conflict: The page is headed '2027 Immerse Education Essay Competition' but states 'The deadline for the current round is 14 January 2026' — 221 days PAST at retrieval. Either the deadline text is stale or the round labelling is. NOT resolved; do not record either date as current.
recommendation: Keep at under_review. If ever surfaced, the record must say the prize is a discount toward the organiser's own open-enrolment £7,495 programme. Recording it as 'scholarship, free to enter' without that would be technically true and materially misleading.

title: Horizon Academic Essay Prize
entry_fee_verbatim: 'No, the Horizon Academic Essay Prize is free for all current high schoolers to participate.'
eligibility_verbatim: 'The competition is open to all students from any country who will be enrolled in high school (as of September 1, 2026).'
prize_structure_verbatim: Grand Visionary: '$1000 USD cash award' + 'Scholarship worth $6450 (USD)'. Grand Innovator: '$500 USD cash award' + 'Scholarship worth $4000 (USD)'. Grand Excellence: '$250 USD cash award' + 'Scholarship worth $3000 (USD)'.
distinction_from_immerse: Horizon awards REAL CASH ($250-$1,000) on top of the programme scholarship. Immerse awards no cash at all. That is a genuine, material difference between two rows a naive 'commercial lead-gen' label would flatten — and it means Horizon's prize retains some value to a student who does not want the organiser's product.
the_same_caveat: The scholarship half is still a discount toward Horizon's own Research Program. The scholarship values ($6,450 / $4,000 / $3,000) also imply the programme's own price is at least $6,450 — a figure the corpus does not hold for Horizon's programme.
deadline_note: 'Submissions Close February 1, 2026, 23:59 PST' — 203 days PAST at retrieval. The next round is not announced on the page.
fair_assessment: Free to enter, worldwide, and pays some real cash. Not harmful. But like Immerse it is primarily a funnel toward a paid programme, and its academic weight is not comparable to a national or international olympiad.
recommendation: Keep at under_review. If surfaced, show the cash and the scholarship separately — they are different kinds of prize and only one is spendable anywhere.

subject: Why `cost` alone cannot classify the commercial tier — and what would
finding: CEO's advice was that finding these rows' prices would let the #154 pay-to-enroll gate work on them automatically. Having researched them, that turns out NOT to be the case for this particular group, and the reason is worth recording.
why: All four essay competitions are **genuinely free to enter**. Their correct `cost` is 0.00. So populating `cost` does not help the gate at all — a cost-based gate will read them as free and let them straight through, which by its own rule is correct: nobody is being asked to pay.
what_actually_distinguishes_them: The thing that makes these different from CERN BL4S — also free, also worldwide — is not price. It is that **the prize is a discount on the organiser's own product**, and in Immerse's case that product is explicitly `open_enrollment`. The competition is free; the pathway it feeds is purchased. A cost column on the COMPETITION cannot express that, because the money is at the other end.
the_shape_in_general: Three distinct things the corpus currently cannot tell apart, all of which can read as cost=0.00: (1) genuinely free and selective — CERN BL4S, TÜBİTAK, CrowdMath; (2) free to enter, prize is a voucher for the organiser's own paid product — Immerse, Horizon; (3) free to enter, prize is money or recognition — most olympiads. Only (2) is a funnel, and it is invisible to a price-based rule.
suggested_signal: The usable discriminator is the relationship between the prize and the organiser: does winning give you something you can spend anywhere, or only something you can spend with the organiser? That is a one-bit property and it is knowable from the prize description, which research already reads. It is NOT derivable from cost, deadline, or selectivity_tier.
honest_scope: This is an observation for whoever owns the gate, not a proposal — I am not going to design a schema change in a research lane. Recording it because I found it while doing what CEO asked and the conclusion was the opposite of the expectation.
